question.worked_solution:
We will use the fact that the dot product is linear.

To quickly compute the numerator $u\cdot (2v),$ we multiply $u\cdot v$ by $2.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot (2v) & =2(u\cdot v) \\  & =2\cdot (-22) \\  & =-44.\end{aligned}
$$

To quickly compute the denominator $u\cdot (5u),$ we compute $u\cdot u$ first and then multiply the result by $5.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot (5u) & =5(u\cdot u) \\  & =5({u}_{1}^{2}+{u}_{2}^{2}+{u}_{3}^{2}+{u}_{4}^{2}) \\  & =5((-2)^{2}+{3}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{4}^{2}) \\  & =5(4+9+1+16) \\  & =5\cdot 30 \\  & =150.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{u\cdot (2v)}{u\cdot (5u)}=\frac{-44}{150}=-\frac{22}{75}.
$$
